components.title: SPARC Application
components.description: SPARC (Systematic Policy and Regulatory Compliance) is a Rails application for managing NIST 800-53 compliance documentation. This component definition covers authentication and access control implementations.

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC implements account management through the User model with active, suspended, and deactivated status enumerations. Administrative users manage accounts via role assignments. The deactivate! and reactivate! methods enforce account lifecycle transitions. Account status changes are audited via AuditEvent logging. Service accounts are managed through a dedicated admin interface with full lifecycle support: create, disable, enable, transfer ownership, and soft-delete. Service account management is restricted to admin users only. Each service account has a designated owner for accountability, and ownership can be transferred between users. Automated service account lifecycle management is provided by ServiceAccountMaintenanceJob, a daily Solid Queue job that auto-disables service accounts with all-expired tokens (reason: token_expired) or exceeding the configurable SPARC_SA_INACTIVITY_DAYS inactivity threshold (default 90 days, reason: inactivity). Proactive email notifications are sent by ServiceAccountNotificationJob, a daily job that detects service accounts approaching token expiry (14-day and 7-day warnings), expired tokens, and approaching inactivity auto-disable thresholds. Notifications are delivered via ServiceAccountMailer to service account owners and all admin users, gated on SparcConfig.enable_smtp? to skip when SMTP is not configured. Instance admin credential rotation (#402/#403) generates AuditEvent rows for every lifecycle event: admin_bootstrap (first install or reset path), admin_credential_synced_from_env (boot-time reconciliation when SM rotated since last task start), admin_credential_rotated (in-task or API-initiated rotation), and admin_password_reset (manual reset via rake task). Account lifecycle guardrails (#878) prevent administrative lockout: the last active administrator cannot be deactivated or suspended by any path, and the break-glass administrator is exempt from the inactivity sweep. Administrative provisioning (#877) issues a SPARC-generated temporary credential that the new account must replace at first sign-in, rather than accepting an administrator-chosen password. See AC-2(3) and IA-5(1). #919 — boundary roster management is delegable rather than admin-only: adding, re-roling and removing members is gated on authorization_boundaries.manage_members, seeded to ISSM/ISSO/SO-ISO and enforced identically on the web and Api::V1 surfaces. The check is boundary-scoped, because an unscoped check matches only instance-level roles and would have refused the delegates it was granted to.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in app/models/user.rb, app/controllers/concerns/authorization.rb, app/controllers/admin/service_accounts_controller.rb, app/jobs/service_account_maintenance_job.rb, app/jobs/service_account_notification_job.rb, and app/mailers/service_account_mailer.rb. Tested by spec/models/user_spec.rb.

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC disables inactive accounts automatically. InactivityCheckJob deactivates accounts whose last sign-in precedes the SPARC_INACTIVITY_DAYS threshold (default 30), selected by the User.inactive_past_threshold scope and applied to human and service accounts alike. Each automatic deactivation writes a system-actor AuditEvent. Two exemptions preserve the availability of administration itself (#878). First, the break-glass administrator -- the account matching SPARC_ADMIN_EMAIL, compared case-insensitively -- is exempt from both inactivity deactivation and password expiry, because that credential is rotated out of band by the sparc-iac Lambda rather than by interactive sign-in; the exemption is scoped to that one account, not to the admin flag, so named administrators remain subject to the sweep. Second, deactivating or suspending the last active administrator is refused outright, by any path, raising User::LastAdminError and recording user_deactivate_refused or user_suspend_refused. Suspension is covered alongside deactivation because a suspended account fails the same active? gate. Both guards are enforced in the User model rather than in a controller, so the automated job, the admin UI, and the REST API inherit them identically.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Rationale for the exemptions: SessionsController#authenticate_local gates on active?, so a deactivated or suspended account cannot authenticate at all, and reactivation requires a second administrator. Disabling the only administrator therefore denies administration with no self-service recovery path -- recovery would require shell access and lib/tasks/admin.rake. The exemptions keep AC-2(3) from defeating AC-2. Note that SPARC_ADMIN_EMAIL is never blank: unset, it falls back to admin@sparc.local, so operators who rename the break-glass account must update the variable or the exemption will protect the wrong address. InactivityCheckJob is not registered in config/recurring.yml and is dormant unless an operator schedules it as docs/ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES.md directs. Implemented in app/models/user.rb, app/jobs/inactivity_check_job.rb, and app/controllers/admin/users_controller.rb. Tested by spec/models/admin_lockout_protection_spec.rb and spec/requests/admin/users_spec.rb.

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC enforces access control through authorize_admin!, authorize_role!, and authorize_permission! controller concerns. The authorization framework supports 57 granular permission keys mapped to resource types and actions. Unauthorized access attempts are blocked and audited. Phase 2 API controllers (control_catalogs, profile_documents, cdef_documents, control_mappings) enforce Bearer token authentication on all endpoints, with admin-only gates on catalog and mapping write operations. The API discovery endpoint (GET /api/v1/available) enforces authorization scoping — callers only see endpoints and HTTP methods they are permitted to use, preventing unauthorized endpoint enumeration. Service account API tokens support endpoint-scoped access via an allowed_endpoints JSONB attribute, restricting each token to a declared set of API paths. Requests to endpoints not in the allowlist are rejected. Service account tokens also enforce CIDR-based IP restrictions, blocking requests from IP addresses outside the configured allowlist. Boundary-to-organization assignment (#770) is governed by a single authorization matrix in BoundaryOrganizationAssigner shared by the admin UI and the Api::V1 endpoint: moving a boundary between organizations is instance-admin-only, while attaching an unassigned boundary requires the org_admin role on the target organization (User#org_admin_of?). The boundary Personnel Roster unifies access records from both user_roles (canonical Role catalog) and legacy authorization_boundary_memberships so no assignment path is hidden. Approving an HDF Amendment is authorized separately from creating one (#809): setting or clearing a scanner-finding disposition requires evidence.write on the boundary, while approving or rejecting it requires Instance Admin or the amendment.approve permission key, which is seeded to the Authorizing Official, Agency Authorizing Official, and ISSM roles and can be granted to any other role from Admin > Roles. All triage and aggregation endpoints remain boundary-scoped. #919 — a sweep of every controller with mutating actions found 14 with no authorization of any kind, including the seven POA&M child controllers, attestations, back-matter resources, boundary environments, profile controls, profile documents, and the API baseline-parameters endpoint. Nesting under a parent did not scope them: each loaded its parent with an unscoped slug lookup, so knowing a slug was sufficient to rewrite POA&M findings, remediation dates, profile baselines and back-matter provenance. All are now gated with authorize_permission! scoped to the owning boundary, mirroring the Api::V1 sibling for each resource. Coverage is enforced structurally rather than by review: a spec enumerates every routed controller with a mutating action and fails when one is neither guarded nor justifiably allowlisted, so a new unguarded controller fails on arrival. Scanners cannot cover this class — they analyse code that exists and cannot flag a guard never written.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in app/controllers/concerns/authorization.rb, app/models/role.rb, app/models/api_token.rb, app/controllers/api/v1/control_catalogs_controller.rb, app/controllers/api/v1/profile_documents_controller.rb, app/controllers/api/v1/cdef_documents_controller.rb, app/controllers/api/v1/control_mappings_controller.rb, app/controllers/api/v1/discovery_controller.rb, and app/controllers/admin/service_accounts_controller.rb. Tested by spec/controllers/ and spec/models/role_spec.rb. Web-layer catalog/baseline/mapping read access is gated by require_authentication_unless_public_controls (app/controllers/concerns/authentication.rb). Conditional coverage: reads are authentication-gated when SPARC_PUBLIC_CATALOGS=false (secure-by-default); set true to intentionally share the control library publicly (#726). Tested by spec/requests/controls_nav_visibility_spec.rb. #770: org-scoped assignment authority uses the org_admin OrganizationMembership role because SPARC has no org-scoped permission catalog; enforced identically in app/services/boundary_organization_assigner.rb for the admin screen and PATCH /api/v1/authorization_boundaries/:id/organization. #809: amendment.approve registered in Role::PERMISSION_KEYS and enforced by Api::V1::FindingDispositionsController#authorize_approve! and HdfTriageController; seeded role grants in db/seeds.rb (PERM_AO, PERM_ISSM).

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC enforces separation of duties through 29 seeded roles: 10 instance-scoped and 19 boundary-scoped. Each role defines a distinct set of permissions preventing any single user from accumulating conflicting privileges. Role assignments are managed by administrators and audited. #919 — promotion authority is split across tiers: a boundary holds back_matter.promote (request) while the instance policy tier holds back_matter.approve_promotion and back_matter.federate (adjudicate), so no role can approve its own promotion request and the review queue cannot be bypassed. Assessors are excluded from back-matter authoring: assessor_3pao holds sap.write and sar.write but no back_matter key, so an assessor cannot edit the provenance it is assessing. Both are pinned by spec so a seed edit cannot silently undo them.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in app/models/role.rb with role seeds in db/seeds/. Tested by spec/models/role_spec.rb.

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC implements least privilege through granular JSONB permission structures defined in Role::PERMISSION_GROUPS. Each role specifies read/write access per resource type (SSP, SAR, CDEF, catalogs, profiles, users). The authorize_permission! method enforces these constraints on every request. Phase 2 API endpoints enforce admin-only gates for catalog and mapping write operations, while profile and CDEF endpoints are accessible to all authenticated users. The API discovery endpoint (GET /api/v1/available) omits write methods for read-only callers and hides entire admin-only endpoints (users, catalog writes, mapping writes) from non-admin users, ensuring the response reflects least-privilege scoping. Service accounts cannot be assigned the admin role, ensuring privileged functions remain restricted to human users. Service account tokens enforce least privilege through endpoint-scoped access (allowed_endpoints JSONB) and CIDR-based IP restrictions, limiting each token to only the API paths and network ranges required for its function. The amendment workflow separates duties within a single disposition record (#809): the person who decides a disposition (decided_by) and the person who approves it (approved_by, approved_at) are captured independently and both are bound into the record's signature_hash. A disposition begins in 'draft' and has no suppressing effect on aggregation or export until an approver acts, so no single actor can both author and activate a suppression without holding the separate amendment.approve permission. #919 — reconciliation of the permission vocabulary found 13 of 35 keys anomalous. Eleven were enforced by code but granted to no role, which (because the admin flag short-circuits permission checks) silently made back-matter authoring, promotion and catalog/profile/CDEF approval instance-admin-only rather than least-privileged. converters.read was granted to seven roles and enforced nowhere, and was removed. Seeds now grant boundary-scoped back-matter to the fourteen boundary roles that already write documents, excluding the assessor, the read-only role and three oversight roles that write no document, so no role gains authority over a compliance artifact that it lacks over the document that artifact supports. admin.rotate_credentials remains admin-only by design.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in app/models/role.rb (PERMISSION_GROUPS), app/controllers/concerns/authorization.rb, and app/controllers/admin/service_accounts_controller.rb. Phase 2 controllers: app/controllers/api/v1/control_catalogs_controller.rb, app/controllers/api/v1/profile_documents_controller.rb, app/controllers/api/v1/cdef_documents_controller.rb, app/controllers/api/v1/control_mappings_controller.rb, app/controllers/api/v1/discovery_controller.rb. Tested by spec/models/role_spec.rb. #809: app/models/finding_disposition.rb (approval_status, approved_by, approved_at, signature_hash), app/controllers/api/v1/finding_dispositions_controller.rb.

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC handles unsuccessful login attempts through session management in the Authentication concern. Failed authentication attempts are logged as audit events with the originating IP address and user agent for monitoring and response.

SPARC provides System Use Notification at two layers. (1) A configurable login consent banner controlled by a single SPARC_BANNER variable (#909), which carries either the notice markup inline or a file: prefixed path to it: when set, a Bootstrap 5 modal presents XSS-sanitized banner content that users must acknowledge before authenticating. A file: prefixed value is never rendered literally, so a mistyped path logs an error and shows no banner rather than displaying the path where the rules of behavior belong. (2) A configurable environment/rules header bar (#682) controlled by SPARC_HEADER_TEXT, SPARC_HEADER_TEXT_COLOR, and SPARC_HEADER_HIGHLIGHT_COLOR, rendered on every screen (pre- and post-login) as escaped plain text describing the deployment environment and rules of behavior. Operator-supplied colors are validated against a strict CSS color grammar (injection guard) but contrast is intentionally operator-owned and not enforced.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Login banner implemented in app/views/sessions/ and app/models/sparc_config.rb. Environment header implemented in app/views/shared/_environment_header.html.erb, app/javascript/controllers/environment_header_controller.js, and app/models/sparc_config.rb (header_text/header_text_color/header_highlight_color/safe_header_color). Conditional coverage: the header is active only when SPARC_HEADER_TEXT is set. Tested by spec/requests/sessions_spec.rb, spec/system/login_banner_spec.rb, spec/models/sparc_config_spec.rb, and spec/views/shared/_environment_header.html.erb_spec.rb.

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC implements session lock via configurable idle timeout controlled by the SPARC_SESSION_TIMEOUT_MINUTES environment variable (default 60 minutes). The check_session_timeout method in the Authentication concern evaluates session freshness on every request and forces re-authentication when the idle threshold is exceeded.

SPARC provides explicit session termination through the logout action. The end_session method resets the Rails session, clears session cookies, and redirects the user to the login page. All session terminations are recorded as audit events.

SPARC controls permitted actions without identification through the SparcConfig.any_auth_enabled? gate. When no authentication providers are enabled, access is restricted to read-only operations. The configuration is enforced at the controller level before any authorization check.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in app/models/sparc_config.rb and app/controllers/concerns/authentication.rb. Tested by spec/models/sparc_config_spec.rb.

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC enforces remote access protection through FORCE_SSL with HSTS enforcement (1 year max-age, includeSubDomains, preload) in the production environment. All remote connections are encrypted via TLS, and unencrypted HTTP requests are automatically redirected to HTTPS. Service account API tokens enforce CIDR-based IP restrictions via the cidr_allowlist attribute, limiting remote API access to approved network ranges.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in config/environments/production.rb and app/models/api_token.rb. Tested by deployment verification.

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC supports multi-factor identification and authentication through multiple configurable providers: local login with bcrypt password hashing, FIDO2/WebAuthn passwordless sign-in (SPARC_FIDO2_ENABLED, #779) where a security key + PIN is app-native MFA in one ceremony (possession + user verification, phishing- and replay-resistant), OIDC with SPARC_OIDC_FORCE_MFA enforcement, LDAP directory authentication, and OAuth (GitHub, GitLab) federation. The Authentication concern orchestrates provider selection and credential verification; WebauthnSessionsController handles the WebAuthn assertion ceremony (credential -> user resolution, signature-counter clone detection). For API access, SPARC supports 3 mutually exclusive auth modes selected via the SPARC_API_AUTH env var: local (SPARC Bearer tokens only), oidc (OIDC JWT only), and hybrid (OIDC JWT for human users, SPARC Bearer tokens restricted to service accounts with the service_account flag). SessionsController blocks service account web login. Boot-time validation in config/initializers/api_auth.rb ensures correct configuration at startup. PIV/CAC smart-card sign-in (SPARC_ENABLE_PIV, #779) consumes a certificate that the mTLS gateway has already validated: PivSessionsController fails closed unless the gateway attests verification via SPARC_PIV_VERIFY_HEADER, then PivAuthService maps the certificate to a provisioned identity. Because HTTP headers cannot carry newlines, gateways forward the PEM URL-encoded, newline-folded, backslash-escaped, or as bare base64 DER; PivAuthService.normalize_pem reassembles all of these before parsing (#824), so a validly presented card is not rejected as absent. A certificate that is missing and one that cannot be decoded are audited as distinct failures, with shape-only diagnostics (byte count, marker and encoding flags) and never the certificate itself.
implemented-requirements.remarks: MFA (IA-2(1)/(2)) is satisfied app-natively by FIDO2/WebAuthn (SPARC_FIDO2_ENABLED, #779) — a security key + PIN, no external IdP required — OR by OIDC with SPARC_OIDC_FORCE_MFA=true delegating to the identity provider. Local-password-only login (SPARC_ENABLE_LOCAL_LOGIN without FIDO2/OIDC) is the break-glass admin path and satisfies identification + single-factor only, NOT MFA. LDAP coverage depends on the directory server's MFA configuration. JWT API authentication requires SPARC_ENABLE_OIDC=true and SPARC_OIDC_ISSUER_URL to be configured. Hybrid mode enforces OIDC for humans and SPARC tokens for service accounts only. Recommended production config: enable OIDC with force MFA, disable local login. Implemented in app/controllers/concerns/authentication.rb, app/controllers/concerns/api_authentication.rb, config/initializers/api_auth.rb, and app/controllers/omniauth_callbacks_controller.rb. Tested by spec/requests/sessions_spec.rb and spec/requests/omniauth_callbacks_spec.rb. See docs/dev/issue_rules.md for the full auth mode coverage matrix.

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC uniquely identifies users via email address with case-insensitive uniqueness validation enforced at both the application and database levels. Each user record has a unique database ID and email, preventing duplicate identifiers across the system. Service accounts are assigned UUID-based identifiers and their API tokens use the sparc_sa_ prefix, enabling clear identification and differentiation of service account tokens from human user tokens in logs and audit records.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Implemented in app/models/user.rb and app/models/api_token.rb. Case-insensitive uniqueness is enforced at the database layer by a functional UNIQUE index on LOWER(email) (migration 20260529000000, #593) in addition to the application-level normalize_email callback and uniqueness validation — the DB index rejects case-variant duplicates even under races or callback-bypassing writes. Tested by spec/models/user_spec.rb.

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC manages authenticator credentials through dual authentication mechanisms: bcrypt password hashing with a minimum length of 12 characters for interactive login, SHA-256 digested SPARC Bearer tokens for API access, and RS256 JWT signature verification for Okta-issued JWTs presented to API endpoints. Password expiry is enforced via the SPARC_PASSWORD_EXPIRY_DAYS configuration (default 30 days), requiring periodic credential rotation. In hybrid mode (SPARC_API_AUTH=hybrid), RS256 JWT is used for human users and SHA-256 token digest for service accounts. Boot-time validation in config/initializers/api_auth.rb ensures correct auth configuration at startup (e.g., OIDC settings present when oidc/hybrid mode selected). JWKS caching uses Rails.cache for multi-process safety. Service account tokens are stored as SHA-256 digests, use the sparc_sa_ prefix for identification, enforce mandatory expiry dates, and track owner accountability. Token regeneration creates a new SHA-256 digest and logs the event. Instance admin credential rotation (#402/#403) is automated through three coordinated mechanisms: (1) bootstrap_admin reconciles the admin password from the SPARC_ADMIN_PASSWORD env var (ECS-injected from Secrets Manager) on every container start, applying any rotation that occurred while the previous task was running; (2) the sparc:rotate_admin_credentials rake task generates a new password and atomically updates both the DB and AWS Secrets Manager via PutSecretValue; (3) POST /api/v1/admin/refresh_credentials accepts a new password from a sparc-iac-managed Lambda (authenticated via service account Bearer token with the admin.rotate_credentials permission) and bcrypts it into the DB. SPARC's task role holds write-only PutSecretValue access on admin-credentials — it cannot read the secret directly, preserving MFA-gated break-glass retrieval through the AWS Console. Initial authenticator issuance at administrative provisioning is SPARC-generated and must be replaced at first sign-in (#877); the break-glass administrator is exempt from password expiry because its credential rotates out of band (#878). See IA-5(1) and AC-2(3).
implemented-requirements.remarks: Full coverage for local login (bcrypt, min 12 chars, expiry). API authenticator management covers both SHA-256 digested SPARC tokens and RS256 JWT signature verification against the OIDC provider's JWKS endpoint. JWT API authentication requires SPARC_ENABLE_OIDC=true and SPARC_OIDC_ISSUER_URL to be configured. When OIDC is enabled, password management for federated users is delegated to the OIDC IdP. LDAP password management is delegated to the directory server. Admin credential rotation (#402/#403) is gated by SPARC_ADMIN_REFRESH_ENABLED=true (off by default — fail closed) and requires sparc-iac counterpart provisioning per risk-sentinel/sparc-iac#197. Implemented in app/models/user.rb, app/models/api_token.rb, app/controllers/concerns/api_authentication.rb, app/controllers/admin/service_accounts_controller.rb, app/services/admin_credential_rotation_service.rb, app/controllers/api/v1/admin/credentials_controller.rb, lib/tasks/admin.rake, and config/initializers/api_auth.rb. Tested by spec/models/user_spec.rb, spec/models/api_token_spec.rb, spec/services/admin_credential_rotation_service_spec.rb, spec/lib/tasks/admin_rake_spec.rb, and spec/requests/api/v1/admin/credentials_spec.rb.

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC enforces password-based authenticator management for local login: bcrypt hashing via has_secure_password, a 12-character minimum aligned to NIST SP 800-63B, expiry governed by SPARC_PASSWORD_EXPIRY_DAYS (default 30), and password_changed_at tracking with a must_reset_password flag that forces replacement before further use. Administrative provisioning issues the initial authenticator rather than accepting one (#877): password and password_confirmation are not permitted attributes in UserProvisioningService, so neither the admin UI nor POST /api/v1/users allows the provisioning administrator to choose the credential. SPARC generates a temporary via User#assign_temporary_password, discloses it exactly once in the creation response, stores only its bcrypt digest, and sets must_reset_password so the user replaces it at first sign-in. This satisfies the IA-5 requirement to change authenticators after initial issuance and ensures no administrator retains knowledge of a credential the user continues to hold. Issuance is audited as admin_temporary_password_issued with provisioning: true, distinct from the user_created event, so 'every credential handed to a user' remains independently queryable.
implemented-requirements.remarks: The rejection of caller-supplied passwords is by omission from the permitted-attribute list rather than by accepting and overwriting them, so a supplied value cannot appear to take effect; note that unpermitted parameters do not raise, so an API client sending a password receives no error -- this is a breaking contract change documented in docs/api/endpoints/users.md and the v1.15.4 release notes. The temporary_password field is present only when local login is enabled (SPARC_ENABLE_LOCAL_LOGIN); on an SSO-only instance there is no local credential to issue and the key is omitted. Self-service registration is unaffected. The break-glass administrator is exempt from expiry (#878; see AC-2(3)). Implemented in app/models/user.rb, app/services/user_provisioning_service.rb, app/controllers/admin/users_controller.rb, and app/controllers/api/v1/users_controller.rb. Tested by spec/requests/admin_provisioning_credential_spec.rb, spec/requests/admin/users_spec.rb, and spec/requests/api/v1/users_spec.rb.

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC supports non-organizational user identification and authentication through OIDC federation with external identity providers including Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, GitHub, and GitLab. The OmniAuth callbacks controller handles federated identity assertions and maps external identities to local user accounts. External users can also authenticate to API endpoints via Okta-issued JWTs, enabling non-organizational user identification for programmatic access without requiring a local SPARC account with a pre-provisioned API token.
implemented-requirements.remarks: CONDITIONAL COVERAGE: Requires SPARC_ENABLE_OIDC=true or OAuth providers enabled. Not met with local-only login (no federation capability). JWT API authentication for external users requires SPARC_ENABLE_OIDC=true and SPARC_OIDC_ISSUER_URL to be configured. Implemented in app/controllers/omniauth_callbacks_controller.rb, app/controllers/concerns/api_authentication.rb, and app/models/sparc_config.rb. Tested by spec/requests/omniauth_callbacks_spec.rb.

implemented-requirements.description: SPARC enforces re-authentication by terminating idle sessions after a configurable timeout period (SPARC_SESSION_TIMEOUT_MINUTES). When the idle threshold is exceeded, the user is redirected to the login page and must re-authenticate to regain access. The timeout is checked on every authenticated request.

SPARC delegates identity proofing to configured OIDC identity providers, which perform identity verification according to their own policies before issuing identity assertions. The application consumes verified identity claims from the provider's token response.
implemented-requirements.remarks: CONDITIONAL COVERAGE: Requires SPARC_ENABLE_OIDC=true. Not met with local-only login (self-registration with no identity proofing). Implemented in app/controllers/omniauth_callbacks_controller.rb. Identity proofing is handled by the external OIDC provider.
